thread:
maria: Heads-up — prod kv-cache started a memory spike on streamers about 15m ago, continuous batching cadence looks off. Observed paging (~2.5x baseline) and a bunch of partial flushes on streaming lanes.
aj: yikes. which cluster? any customer errors?
maria: us-east-1/cluster-7. Some clients saw stalled tokens and 502/timeout retries from the proxy. infra metrics: KV cache resident > 95% and paging rate +300%.
srinivas: grabbing logs. seeing a pattern: large concat keys with repeated prefix hits causing batch growth; batch window didn't cut in because cadence timer stalled.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall — taking. will start by throttling continuous batching and evicting oversized entries.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-221 (severity: high) — paging spike on kv-cache, streaming token stalls — monitoring channel #incidents-ops.
product-ops: any customer impact yet? do we need to notify CS?
amelia: a few PLG customers reported partial responses and an increase in latency around 11:12. CS is seeing ~12 ticket pings. recommend a short status note.
aj: proposed immediate mitigations:
1) reduce continuous_batch_max_tokens from 1024 -> 256
2) enable aggressive kv-eviction for keys older than 30s
3) temporarily disable cross-request prefix caching for streaming lanes
can we hotpatch config?
oncall-sre: applying 1 & 2 now. watch logs for OOMs.

deploy-bot: rolling config change on cluster-7: set continuous_batch_max_tokens=256

srinivas: logs after change: batch sizes dropped, but partial flush bug still appears — some streams show cadence gaps where token delivery pauses for 700-1200ms then resumes.
dmitri: that's the partial flush bug we saw in canaries last month — sequence: large batch flush triggers a KV paging compaction path that yields while GC runs.
amelia: do we need to rollback something or patch runtime?
oncall-sre: short term: force a KV compaction cooldown and restart runtime workers on the three affected nodes. doing one node at a time.

maria: jotting commands for the restart (one-at-time):
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime-7 --grace-period=60 --timeout=5m
watch kubectl get pods -l app=serving-runtime-7 -o wide
```

aj: also pushed an emergency tweak to the streaming cadence scheduler to avoid gap amplification:
```
streaming.cadence.min_interval_ms=12  # from 8
streaming.partial_flush_threshold=32  # from 16
```
oncall-sre: started restarts at node-a. monitoring traces. paging rate trending down.

srinivas: customer-impact snapshot: ~0.8% of active streams experienced token pauses >500ms, tail p50->p95 latency delta increased ~220ms. no data loss observed, but transient 502s for a small subset when proxy retried.
product-ops: prepping customer note template + AM outreach for top 10 accounts.

deploy-bot: rollout complete on node-a. node-a metrics: resident mem -18%, paging -40%.
oncall-sre: moving to node-b.
amelia: quick question — did the earlier change to continuous_batch_max_tokens cause any regressions elsewhere? metrics look clean for embeddings lanes.
aj: so far embeddings unaffected. text-gen lanes improved.
dmitri: next steps after stabilization:
- postmortem to root-cause batching config + key size growth
- add guardrails: per-key size cap and batch budget enforcement
- add early detectors for cadence stalls (traces + metric alert)

maria: for now, monitoring looks stable across cluster-7. paging back to baseline. will leave throttles in place for 2 hours and then gradually roll to default with canary.
oncall-sre: handing off to daytime oncall — @srinivas please take watch for the next 2 hours.
srinivas: taking handoff. will follow up with a timeline for hotfix PR and postmortem.

product-ops: CS note queued. will update customers in 30m. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-221 status: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned: srinivas. Severity downgraded to medium.

maria: thanks everyone — big help. logging actions for postmortem.
aj: adding reproduction snippet to the ticket for the ops/infra team.

srinivas: filing tracker: GH #5020 with initial hypothesis and logs.

-- end of thread --
